BOT ANALYSIS

Adaptive Gumbel Guide v13.5.1 is the strongest established version. It uses Gumbel guidance only when the evidence is complete and keeps every legal move available to its search.
Rules and test-edition choices

Win by occupying all four center-garden corners, or enclosing the whole center garden in a friendly harmony. The four corners have golden rings.

Drop at an empty starting gate, or the same green field as a friendly flower, provided your Chysalith count there is at least the opponent’s. Ties, including zero against zero, are allowed for both players. Water must touch a field and remains in its home field. Gates are amber; fields green; rivers blue.

Harmony needs a closed boundary of at least four compatible friendly flowers with clear orthogonal sight lines. Blue or purple lines show valid links; shaded areas show closed loops. Disharmonizing friendly flowers cannot contribute. Enemy Chysalith sight can break links. Boundary flowers remain capturable; enemy flowers trapped inside a zone cannot move.

Star pairs: Water, Sun, Daisy. Sun: Star, Shining, Clover. Clover: Sun, Daisy, Water. Daisy: Clover, Shining, Star. Shining: Sun, Daisy, Water. Water: Shining, Clover, Star. Chysalith harmonizes with every friendly flower. Disharmony: Star–Clover, Star–Shining, Sun–Water, Sun–Daisy, Clover–Shining, Daisy–Water.

Movement follows the main-branch game: fixed-step flowers may move up to their step count. Every movement action must change the flower’s intersection; passing/staying in place is not legal. Captures remove the victim; they do not add it to your hand. Picking up your Sun uses a turn.

This edition uses actual simple bounded harmony loops instead of convex hulls, keeps the website implementation’s tied-count field access, and enforces enemy-harmony and Water restrictions along movement paths. Harmony tracing removes bridges, checks actual simple boundaries in both orientations, and rejects self-crossing boundaries. Unusual crossing-link networks still require further testing. Bot plans are heuristics, not proofs of a forced win.

The previous Strategic v5 style keeps the established evaluation and adds a bounded forcing-threat proof search at Standard thinking time or longer. Full planning adds multi-flower enclosure estimates and phase-sensitive pattern evaluation, and remains experimental because larger stress comparisons have not established a consistent advantage. Reversible search and embedded WebAssembly are available for experiments; neither is enabled by default. The bot uses time-limited selective search with exhaustive immediate-win scans where completed, progressive root widening, cached positions, history ordering, conservative late-move reductions, tactical continuation search, graph-based one-bend enclosure plans, forced-defense continuation search, persistent successor and move-order reuse, and bounded exact solving when reserves are empty. V4 enclosure plans consider up to two missing flowers and ten boundary vertices, with bounded candidate generation and approximate arrival costs; they are estimates, not exhaustive planning. The experimental Exploratory style uses heuristic-guided Monte Carlo tree search; no neural network is included. The development lab offers outcome-based SPSA tuning of connectivity, mobility, initiative, reserves, and vulnerability patterns, with separate validation. Automatic acceptance requires at least 12 decisive validation games, a 95% Wilson lower bound above 50%, and passing tactical checks at a suitable thinking budget. V6 knowledge tuning uses the same minimum decisive-game and confidence requirements. Training is explicit and runs only when you start it. Depth counts individual turns. Thinking time is a target; completing a move-generation batch can take longer. No Elo or expert-strength claim has been established. Repetition is illegal: a move may not recreate any earlier complete position with the same side to move (situational superko). No legal actions draws. If one action produces center control for both players, the moving player wins.

Old v1 and v2 saves can be loaded. Multi-step plans have bounded candidate generation and approximate travel costs; they do not prove that a construction survives enemy replies. The forcing solver proves only completed winning searches, checks every legal defense at opponent nodes, and otherwise reports unknown. The included opening suggestions were checked for immediate opposing wins and affect ordering only. Exact solving reports unknown when its budget or depth limit is reached. Save your difficult positions to use as regression puzzles or send for further bot improvements. Everything is included in this file: no downloads, fonts, images, servers, or account required. Your game is saved automatically where your browser permits local storage; Save game works as a portable backup. Changing color starts a new game.

Research and validation

V7 offers a conservative candidate that preserves v6’s evaluation and strategic selection while checking immediate wins before static leaf evaluation, filtering impossible immediate wins before expensive ordering, computing move priorities once, and reusing verified successor-key prefixes. Additional experimental modes offer staged root generation and widening, persistent move ordering, protected tactical reductions, wider root selection, a bounded depth-first proof-number solver, and hybrid MCTS with separate minimax backups. The proof solver includes every legal defender reply, permits a small set of quiet attacker preparations, and reports unknown when unsuccessful or unfinished. These alternative algorithms have not established superior match strength. Search depth is selective, not an exhaustive proof. Frozen v6 remains available. V7 knowledge tuning is explicit and retains the original weights unless separate validation satisfies its acceptance criteria.

V7 validation: the released conservative candidate won 1 game, lost 0, drew 0, and left 3 unfinished against frozen v6 in four games at a 600 ms requested target and a 120-turn cap, with swapped colors and isolated JavaScript VM contexts. This is a small exploratory sample and does not establish overall superiority or Elo. Earlier selective candidates scored 2 wins / 0 losses / 2 unfinished in four 400 ms games, then 3 wins / 1 loss / 2 unfinished in six 600 ms games; the final selective candidate scored 1 win / 2 losses / 1 unfinished in four 800 ms games. It was not promoted. The wider-root variant left all four 400 ms games unfinished; hybrid MCTS scored 0 wins / 1 loss / 1 unfinished in two 600 ms games. Thinking targets are not hard deadlines; actual elapsed times were recorded. Unfinished games are not wins or draws.

All four main candidates (conservative, selective, wider-root, and hybrid MCTS) passed the 33-check tactical suite. Conservative search preserved a quiet exhaustive depth-three score of 178 and detected an independently verified three-turn win at depth two with tactical continuation disabled, while v6 returned a positional score. This isolates the improved leaf check; it does not mean v6 cannot find that win with its normal forcing solver. Successor-prefix reuse matched 192 reference and make/undo checks. Optimized threat checks matched v6 on 54 sampled midgame checks, taking 896.7 ms versus 979.8 ms in that component workload, about 9% less time; this is not a whole-engine speed claim. The proof-number solver’s five-turn winning action was independently checked against 32 first defenses and 32 follow-up defenses, and repetition, node-cap, parent-preservation, and low-memory checks passed. It did not demonstrate a speed advantage over the existing forcing solver and stays experimental.

The shipped HTML’s worker code was exercised using isolated worker threads with a minimal DOM/canvas adapter: engine selection, alternating bot turns, single-step, pause and cancellation, undo, saved-game restoration, and human-play resumption passed. Comparison-lab routing also passed. A fresh native-browser run was unavailable in this execution environment; earlier v6 browser/mobile checks apply to the preserved interface. No new learned weights were adopted. V7 outcome-based tuning is available when explicitly started; it uses separate validation openings and tactical checks before accepting weights.

V6 adds principal-variation search with full re-search of promising narrow-window results, transposition move ordering across iterative depths, repetition-aware forcing proofs up to seven turns, optional selective successor generation and root evaluation with progressive widening, and handcrafted evaluation of legal capture vulnerability, garden-corner reach, and contested enclosure completion squares. Selective search retains immediate-win checks and widens alternatives but does not exhaustively evaluate every strategic move. Learning uses outcome-based SPSA; it has no neural network. Each tuning run has separate validation openings and tactical checks, and keeps its original weights unless enough decisive validation games support changing them.

Final v6 validation against frozen v5 used ten new games with swapped colors, isolated browser workers, and equal requested thinking time. Eight games used 800 ms targets with an 80-turn cap; two used 3000 ms targets with a 64-turn cap. Results: 4 wins, 0 losses, 0 draws, 6 unfinished games. Unfinished games are not wins or draws; this sample does not establish Elo or statistical superiority. Earlier combined-mode screening produced 3 wins and 1 loss in four games. All four search/evaluation variants passed the 33-check tactical suite. Additional checks covered search score parity, losing positions, repetition-aware proofs, parent-state preservation, color symmetry, and low-memory legality. A five-turn forcing-win fixture was independently checked against 36 first defenses and 56 follow-up defenses. In an equal-budget, cold-cache test, v5’s forcing solver reported unknown after 1 second; v6 proved the win within that budget. A small non-neural tuning run did not establish better weights, so the original weights were retained. Recommended v6 combines selective search with opponent-aware evaluation. Previous bot v5 remains available.

V5 preserves the established strategic evaluation and forcing solver. It caches fixed board geometry, repeated arrival costs, and special-piece status, computes ordering priorities once per move, and filters geometrically impossible immediate wins before full simulation. Previous bot · v4.1 restores the prior search and hot paths for comparison. Game rules are the same for both versions.

V5 validation: 61,504 alignment pairs and all board rays/neighbors matched the reference; 192 cached-evaluation and make/undo comparisons and all 33 tactical checks passed. Its immediate-win geometry filter matched full simulation over 21,126 actions from 34 positions, with both owners tested. The same evaluation workload over 22 sampled positions took 5.11 seconds in v4.1 and 4.06 seconds in v5 (26% greater throughput on the development machine). In eight paired-color games at a 400 ms requested move budget and an 80-turn cap, v5 scored 4 wins, 2 losses, and 2 unfinished games. A separate four-game comparison at 800 ms and a 96-turn cap scored 2 wins and 2 losses. Total: 6 wins, 4 losses, 2 unfinished. Searches ran sequentially with isolated persistent caches and equal requested time. In the 400 ms set, mean actual elapsed time was 432 ms for v5 and 503 ms for v4.1; requested time is a target, not a hard deadline. The three-turn forcing-win fixture also passed against all 46 legal defenses under the current tied-count rules. These are small development samples and do not establish statistical superiority or Elo. Evaluation weights and rules remain unchanged; rejected search rewrites are not included.

Connection and enclosure planning draws on ideas from MoHex (Hex) and Castro (Havannah). The tactical engine uses general alpha-beta techniques also found in Stockfish. The optional Monte Carlo style uses handcrafted priors and progressive widening. These projects inspired the approach; their game-specific strength does not transfer to Sho Dan Sho.

MoHex 2.0 research · Castro · Stockfish search · KataGo graph-search notes

Development checks include 16 rule/tactical regressions, 288 make/undo comparisons against the reference simulator (including legal moves, parent isolation, harmony geometry, and field information), a 33-check portable tactical suite, an independently verified three-turn forcing win, and loss-to-puzzle extraction. Two unique defenses recovered from losing match traces and a three-turn forcing win verified against 46 legal replies under the current tied-count rules are available in Practice a defense. Review can add verified defensive positions to your local collection. Paired matches use color swaps and equal thinking time. A 200-game development stress comparison of full planning against v3 at an 80 ms target per move produced 67 wins, 70 losses, and 63 unfinished games. This did not justify changing the default evaluation. The test used paired colors, varied seeded openings, a 64-turn cap, and concurrent execution; it does not establish an Elo rating or performance at normal thinking times. Default evaluation weights remain unchanged.

The file itself remains offline; these optional reference links require internet. Non-neural tuning uses a small SPSA experiment: Stockfish testing and SPSA. No third-party engine source was copied.

v12 Virtual Harmony · superko and must-play search

V12 removes passing and replaces threefold-repetition draws with situational superko: any move that recreates an earlier complete position with the same player to move is illegal. The rule is enforced by the shared move generator, save/restore history, bot workers, tactical search, and human legal-move UI.

The recommended engine adds virtual-harmony bridge analysis, opponent must-play blocking squares, garden-corner urgency, connection-aware move ordering and evaluation, a larger persistent superko-aware endgame proof search, and an experimental progressive-widening PUCT engine with lightweight AMAF/RAVE updates for deployment and critical connection moves. The comparison lab uses a 400-ply default for v12-v11 tests.

Validation: v12 passed all 33 legacy tactical checks at the 800 ms UI budget. In a representative 264-action opening, the v12 must-play guide let the proven hybrid complete depth 2 in roughly the same 800 ms in which v11 completed depth 1, while selecting the same move. The experimental progressive-widening PUCT considered all 264 legal actions but initially widened to 34 and completed 106 simulations in about 800 ms. A 120-ply rule walk produced zero stay-in-place moves and zero repeated positions. Across 22 saved game positions at 800 ms, v12 and v11 agreed on 21 moves; the one disagreement disappeared at a 10-second reference search, so no Elo or statistically significant head-to-head advantage is claimed yet. V11 remains selectable as the frozen previous baseline.

v11 deep tactical engine · search and safety changes

V11 contains a new independent alpha-beta/PVS tactical engine and a conservative recommended hybrid. The recommended mode retains the frozen v10 principal at short time controls, then applies v11 whole-position capture verification; at longer time controls the independent v11 search also challenges the principal. This avoids throwing away a proven baseline while the newer positional model is still being validated.

The independent v11 engine uses state-dependent piece values, dynamic square evaluation, exact legal capture maps plus legal hypothetical-square attack maps, whole-position all-capture root safety, bounded tactical-graph continuation, threat extensions, Sho Dan Sho-specific quiescence, adaptive width, aspiration windows, compact transposition hashing, history/killer ordering, and a compact value/policy head. With empty reserves it also invokes a bounded repetition-aware exact proof search and uses a completed proof over heuristic evaluation.

Parallel deep v11 root-splits the legal root moves across up to four browser workers. Policy PUCT v11 uses the same evaluation/policy features with Monte-Carlo graph search. Both remain experimental. The previous v10 and v9 engines remain selectable for controlled comparison.

Final build validation: at 800 ms, frozen v10, recommended v11, independent deep v11, and incremental cursor v11 each passed all 33 tactical regression checks. A paired late-game screen against frozen v10 used four reserve-empty validation positions with color/engine assignment swapped: at 250 ms, v11 scored 0 wins, 0 losses, 6 draws, and 2 unfinished games; a further paired test at the UI's 800 ms Quick budget scored 0 wins, 0 losses, and 2 draws. These tests establish tactical parity and no observed head-to-head regression in this sample, not an Elo or overall-strength advantage. Two root-split worker shards also returned legal independent candidates in the parallel-worker harness. The SPSA feature tuner completed a smoke test and correctly refused to adopt weights without decisive validation.

v9 capture fix · ten-game validation

The Clover-feeding bug was reproduced in v8: with an enemy Clover at 5,4, v8 dropped a Chysalith at 4,4 for an uncompensated capture. V9 checks legal enemy captures before a root move becomes eligible, including the earliest Stop thinking fallback. It rejects unsupported exposure of the moved or newly dropped flower when a safe alternative is available. Necessary defensive sacrifices and exact wins receive separate treatment.

Exchange checks follow legal captures and recaptures, including recapture bait, for up to four further plies and a bounded node count. Incomplete continuations receive conservative bounds instead of invented recapture credit. Values consider actual mobility, harmony links and boundaries, Clover relay partners, Sun protection, frozen or paused pieces, and replacement scarcity. The evaluation adjustment is modest and handcrafted. Ordinary captures now trigger tactical leaf search even outside garden fights; root reply screens retain all captures and credit verified recapture opportunities.

Final ten-game result against frozen released v8: 1 wins, 1 losses, 6 draws, 2 unfinished. Five new seeded openings were each played with swapped colors. Both engines requested 800 ms per move, width 12, with a 200-ply limit after four random opening drops. Each game used fresh isolated VM contexts; the candidate was frozen before testing. Unfinished games are separate, and there is no score-based adjudication. Actual move times can exceed the target during required initial scanning and safety checks.

Actual mean thinking time: v9 827.4 ms; v8 804.7 ms. Mean completed selective depth: v9 1.09; v8 1.17. The focused tests establish the reproduced capture fix; this small comparison does not establish an overall rating gain or strength at longer time controls.

v10 dynamic tactical upgrade · validation

V10 keeps the released v9 rule engine and selective-search framework while replacing the fixed-only tactical valuation layer with role-aware material values and dynamic piece-square scoring. Reserve scarcity, mobility, active harmony, special-piece status, game phase, garden/corner relevance, field access, open rays, harmony and disharmony partners, Clover relays, Sun–Chysalith protection, Shining pressure on Chysaliths, Chysalith pressure on Suns and harmony pieces, and cached enemy reach can all change a flower’s effective value.

Root safety now examines the whole friendly position after a candidate, rather than only the flower that moved or was dropped. Legal enemy captures are ranked and followed through bounded capture/recapture continuations. If the exchange budget expires, unverified recaptures receive no credit, so an unfinished calculation cannot make a hanging move look safe.

Focused regression: in a deterministic midgame position, v9 chose Chysalith to 2,13. The whole-position exchange audit found 68.7 points of newly created uncompensated exposure elsewhere in the position (86.7 worst immediate tactical loss from a zero-exposure baseline). V10 rejected that line and selected a zero-exposure alternative. A separate recapture fixture produced an exact bounded exchange value of +171.45 and v10 immediately recaptured on 4,9 with the Star from 4,13.

Checks: all 33 existing tactical tests passed. A short four-game paired-color smoke comparison against v9 at a deliberately tiny requested 20 ms budget and 40-ply cap produced 1 v10 win, 0 losses, 0 draws, and 3 unfinished games. Both engines completed only selective depth 1 in this stress setting, and actual root-scan times exceeded the tiny requested target, so this is a routing/regression check rather than an Elo or overall-strength claim. Use the Development Lab’s v10 vs v9 comparison for longer local testing.

v8 validation · 20 games against v7

Streaming v8: 9 wins, 5 losses, 5 draws, 1 unfinished against the previous recommended conservative v7. All 20 scheduled games were run. Ten seeded openings were each played with swapped colors; each opening started with four random legal drops. Both engines requested 400 ms per turn at width 12, with a 200-ply cap after the opening. Each game used fresh isolated engine contexts. The candidate was frozen before the test, and every played action was checked for legality. Unfinished games are excluded from win-rate claims.

Actual mean thinking time: v8 402.1 ms; v7 403.8 ms. Mean completed selective depth: v8 1.06; v7 1.08. These depths are selective, not exhaustive. The positive score supports trying v8 as the default, but 20 games at one short time control do not establish an overall rating gain or strength at 3–30 seconds.

The new search constructs interior successors only when visited, uses geometry-filtered immediate-win checks, extends threatened leaf positions through bounded forced defenses, and protects captures and harmony changes from late reductions. The existing strategic evaluation and initial root move scan are retained. All 33 tactical checks passed, as did the known three-turn winning sequence and an exhaustive quiet-position score comparison. Every one of the 2,136 played moves and all 20 outcomes were independently replayed with the reference rules implementation.

QUICK HEAD-TO-HEAD

Fair wall-clock paired-color screening for experimental Adaptive Gumbel v13.5.1 against frozen FastVC v13.2. It uses identical paired openings, keeps unfinished games separate, and omits full move traces so 20-game iteration tests are lighter. Keep the same seed when comparing engine revisions.

Ready. Fair-time Part 2: 20 games · 800 ms search · 1000 ms hard cap · 400 plies. Gumbel is skipped on roots it cannot fully probe; when active it only guides ordering and the full v13.2 legal root remains searchable.

Result format includes W/L/D/unfinished, decisive win rate, color split, actual mean think time, mean search depth, plies, and final on-board material for every game. This makes regressions much easier to diagnose than a headline score alone.

v12.2 tuning · held-out match validation

v12.2 keeps the v12 no-pass and situational-superko rules. The accepted engine replaces root-only Virtual Harmony guidance with v12 evaluation and move ordering throughout the proven v11 tactical search, while using geometry-filtered exact-win/threat scans to recover search time.

Tactical regression: 33/33 passed at the 800 ms Quick setting. Earlier tuning variants that weakened tactical coverage or lost match screens were rejected.

Two independent short-control paired-color screens against frozen v12 favored the integrated candidate: an earlier screen finished 5 wins / 1 loss among completed games, and a fresh held-out screen finished 5 wins / 2 losses / 1 unfinished. A longer 800 ms confirmation produced a completed v12.2 win before the remaining long games exceeded the external test harness time window. These samples support promotion as the strongest tested candidate here, but they are not an Elo claim.

The development lab keeps frozen v12 selectable so larger local 800 ms / 3 s / 10 s comparisons can continue under identical rules.

v13 FastVC · real virtual connections

FastVC v13 replaces the old one-square Virtual Harmony heuristic with an H-search/FastVC-inspired connection engine. It stores minimal VC and VSC carrier sets between typed harmony endpoints, combines serial connections with an AND rule, combines alternative semi-connections with an OR rule, tracks alternative carriers, and derives structural must-play intersections. Because Sho Dan Sho allows captures and movement, structural VC proofs are explicitly separated from rule-engine proofs: structural carriers guide evaluation and move ordering, while only exhaustively verified immediate defenses may hard-prune.

Two goal layers are evaluated at once: a Harmony Connection Graph for enclosure scaffolding around the central garden, and a Four-Corner Connectivity Graph for distinct corner-access plans. Every reported connection includes endpoints, required empty intersections, compatible piece kinds, capture vulnerability, enemy pressure on carrier squares, and alternative carriers.

Part 2 · v13.3 experimental: Gumbel-Top-k and Sequential Halving now reduce the huge root action space before the tactical verifier. The Gumbel sample is deterministic per full superko-aware state for reproducible testing. Because the current policy/value are handcrafted rather than learned, Sho Dan Sho keeps several halving survivors and lets the proven tactical verifier choose among them instead of trusting a single statistical winner blindly.
